messages:
alex: Heads-up: we're planning a small schema migration for notifications_preference (add 'digest' enum) during tonight's change window (22:00-23:00 UTC). It includes a short online column add + a backfill for ~12M rows. Deploybot will schedule a canary.

jamie: timeline? is the backfill online or a maintenance job?

alex: online ADD COLUMN with default NULL, then backfill in batches with our backfill service. We'll use advisory locks to avoid concurrent writers. No downtime intended.

lei: we need to pin the service that writes new rows to schema v2 while backfill runs, otherwise we'll have mix of NULLs and enums. Suggest pinning canary to image tag v2.3.1 for 30m.

natalie: agree on pinning. Also can we run a small dry-run on staging with the same batch size? production row distribution looks skewed by tenant.

deploy-bot: @alex scheduled deploy window: 2026-05-14 22:00 UTC. Canary at 22:05. To confirm, react with :white_check_mark:.

alex: :white_check_mark: starting preflight checklist at 21:30.

jamie: checklist items: 1) schema migration SQL 2) backfill job config 3) alert thresholds + SLOs 4) rollback / escape hatch 5) traffic pinning plan. I added a PR with the SQL.

lei: copy of SQL for quick review:
```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE notifications ADD COLUMN preference TEXT; -- ENUM comes via check constraint in followup
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_notifications_pref ON notifications(preference);
COMMIT;

-- backfill pattern (pseudo)
UPDATE notifications
SET preference = 'digest'
WHERE preference IS NULL AND id BETWEEN $start AND $end;
```

natalie: concern: UPDATE will create WAL spikes. We should use chunked updates at 5k rows with sleep and max 4 concurrent workers. Also consider using UPDATE .. WHERE id IN (...) to avoid full scans.

jamie: we'll run the backfill service which uses outline-chunking and pauses on cpu/memory pressure; set concurrency 4, batch 5k, rate limit 200 updates/s.

alex: rollback plan: 1) pause backfill service; 2) set feature flag notifications:v2=false (immediately stop writers using enum); 3) revert schema only if emergency (drop column). Prefer to pause writers + resume.

lei: we should also pin the runtime library that performs serialization. If the writer sees unknown enum value it fails. So we'll add compatibility layer: writers will write string values for now and migration will normalize. That avoids hard fails.

natalie: monitoring: set alert if update latency > 200ms or if replication lag > 30s or if backfill error rate > 0.5%. I added traces in datadog and an SRE runbook link.

sre-bot: added incident channel #incidents-migrations and created pager schedule for oncall. Paging threshold: error_rate > 1% for 5m.

jamie: small canary plan: deploy app v2.3.1 to 2% of traffic at 22:05, start schema ADD at 22:10, once DDL completes (should be near-instant) start backfill on 1% of rows for 15m. If all green, ramp to 10% (22:30) and continue.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: job_id=cb-9042, target=2%. Logs: pulling image v2.3.1.

alex: running preflight checks now: CHECK 1: migration SQL reviewed? yes. CHECK 2: migration backup snapshot taken (pg_basebackup at 21:40) yes. CHECK 3: read replicas caught up? replication lag 0s.

lei: starting DDL (non-blocking) in 3...2...

deploy-bot: DDL job completed: ALTER TABLE finished. Duration 12s.

jamie: starting backfill on 1% sample with concurrency 1. batch_size=5000.

natalie: saw first batch successful. CPU 12% on writer hosts. WAL throughput normal. No replication lag.

lei: expanding backfill to 4 workers and enabling circuit-breaker checks.

alex: we need to pin services in prod routes: route svc-notifications -> image v2.3.1 pinned for canary. ops, please confirm route pin applied.

deploy-bot: route pin applied for svc-notifications to v2.3.1 for canary traffic.

jamie: alert: backfill error rate spiked to 0.8% for 1 min, most errors are constraint violations due to unexpected existing value 'weekly_digest'. Investigating.

lei: those are older values, fixable. We'll add a normalization step to treat 'weekly_digest' as 'digest' in the updater. Patching backfill job now.

natalie: normalize patch deployed to backfill service. reprocessing failing chunks. error rate falling.

jamie: conditions to ramp: error_rate < 0.2% for 10m, replication_lag < 10s, 95p latency < 120ms. We're at 0.05% and 95p latency 98ms. Ready to ramp to 10%.

alex: ramp approved. Also set pin on all writer pods to v2.3.1. Do we need a DB-level advisory lock during critical chunk ranges?

lei: we'll acquire advisory lock per tenant id range when updating hot tenants to avoid concurrent writes. Backfill service supports that.

deploy-bot: traffic ramp to 10% complete. canary.id=cb-9042 -> 10%.

jamie: ongoing monitoring looks fine. marking milestone: canary_stage=passed. schedule main backfill to start at 23:00 with concurrency 4 and throttle to 200 updates/s.

natalie: note: set PG statement_timeout=60s for backfill worker to avoid long-running locks. Also ensure vacuum is scheduled after heavy updates.

alex: last call for objections before main backfill kickoff at 23:00?

lei: no objections.

jamie: starting full backfill now. jobs spawning.

sre-bot: alert: replication lag bumped to 21s for 2m. Triggering mild throttling on backfill.

natalie: throttling engaged: backfill concurrency -> 2, rate -> 120 updates/s. monitoring continuing.

jamie: we hit a secondary issue: a tenant with a long-running transaction blocked vacuum. Pausing that tenant's chunks and moving on. open ticket #INC-947.

alex: action items: 1) continue throttled backfill 2) follow-up with tenant owner in morning to resolve long tx 3) keep feature pin 30m after backfill completes, then gradually unpin.

deploy-bot: Backfill progress: 57% complete. ETA 45m at current throttle.

lei: decision: we will not drop the old column or add strict enum constraint for 48 hours. Keep compatibility mode. That gives us time to monitor.

jamie: leaving post-mortem notes: observed higher replication lag than predicted for short period; improved by throttling. Add new preflight to simulate heavy-update WAL to estimate safe throttle.

alex: thanks team. final note: if anything spikes above thresholds, pause backfill immediately and we'll coordinate rollback/hard stop. Otherwise we'll do a controlled finish and then remove pins after 30m stabilization.

deploy-bot: Backfill job cb-9042 completed: 100% rows updated. Duration 1h2m. No rollback performed. :tada:
